# FSOT-2.1-Instruct-0.5B

**FSOT 2.1 Instruct (0.5B)** — open instruct model derived from
[`Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct) with
**FSOT-guided pathway post-training** (isolated math / MCQ / code / ontology
LoRAs, domain-map routing during research training, anti-poison gates).

This release is a **single dense checkpoint** (pathway LoRAs weighted-merged
then `merge_and_unload`) so it loads with standard:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("PATH_OR_HUB_ID", trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("PATH_OR_HUB_ID", trust_remote_code=True)
```

Compatible with **lm-evaluation-harness**, Hugging Face model hub upload,
and Kaggle Models / notebooks.

## Method (short)

- Base: Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct
- Training: pathway-isolated LoRA (r=8) on FSOT-routed curricula
- Research system keeps adapters separate at inference (anti-poison)
- **Leaderboard export**: weighted merge of pathway adapters → merge into base
- FSOT influence: foundational seeds / domain map / D_eff routing during train;
  release is a standard causal LM

### Merge weights used for this file

```json
{
  "ontology": 0.08,
  "math": 0.25,
  "mcq": 0.35,
  "code": 0.32
}
```

Source pathway set: `C:\Users\damia\Desktop\fsot 2.1 llm\llm\models\pathway_adapters\20260717T130125Z_deepen_mcq`

### Internal refine-loop scores (n≈16, not official leaderboard)

| Pack | Accuracy |
|------|----------|
| gsm8k | 25.0% |
| arc_easy | 75.0% |
| mmlu | 68.8% |
| humaneval | 93.3% |

These are **not** lm-eval full-set numbers. Run the official harness before claiming leaderboard results.

## Intended use

- Small-model instruct / code / science QA experiments
- Baseline for FSOT routing research vs merged export
- Community leaderboard submissions (after full lm-eval)

## Limitations

- 0.5B parameter scale — not frontier SOTA overall
- Merged export can lag the multi-adapter research stack on some packs
- Math (GSM8K) remains the weakest pathway in refine loops
- Always report **full harness** numbers, not n=16 refine scores

## License

Apache-2.0 for this merge packaging and adapters contribution, subject to the
base model license (Qwen). Cite both.

## Citation

```
@software{fsot_21_instruct_05b,
  title  = {FSOT 2.1 Instruct 0.5B},
  year   = {2026},
  note   = {Derived from Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct with FSOT pathway post-training}
}
```

## Smoke

```json

  "prompt": "Complete the Python function. Output code only.\n\ndef add(a, b):\n",
  "completion_preview": "```python\ndef add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n```",
  "dtype": "torch.bfloat16",
  "device": "cuda:0"
}
```

# FSOT 2.1 Instruct 0.5B (PyTorch / Transformers)

## Load on Kaggle

`python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import torch

# Kaggle mounts the model here after you Attach the model to the notebook:
path = "/kaggle/input/fsot-21-instruct-05b/pytorch/transformers/1"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path, trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    path, torch_dtype=torch.float16, device_map="auto", trust_remote_code=True
)
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a Python function that adds two numbers."}]
text = tok.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
inputs = tok(text, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=128, do_sample=False)
print(tok.decode(out[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]:], skip_special_tokens=True))
`

#### **🌾*****AgroVision-AI: End-to-End Deep Learning Pipeline for Agricultural Intelligence****
### **🚀 Project Overview**
**AgroVision-AI **is a production-ready, full-stack computer vision application designed to optimize crop yield and prevent agricultural losses through automated disease detection and plant health diagnostics. Moving past the limitations of traditional, localized models, AgroVision-AI deploys an optimized convolutional neural network (CNN) integrated seamlessly into a lightweight, responsive web ecosystem. The platform enables farmers, researchers, and autonomous greenhouse systems to upload crop imagery and receive real-time, actionable diagnostic reports.
**### 🧠 Core Architecture & Technical Layout. **
1. The Deep Learning Engine (TensorFlow/Keras)
The core classification mechanism utilizes a customized Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture optimized for localized plant tissue feature extraction:
> Feature Extraction Layer: Sequential 2D Convolutional layers coupled with Max-Pooling operations to systematically downsample spatial dimensions while preserving critical edge, texture, and color anomaly features.
> Regularization & Stability: Integrated Dropout layers and Batch Normalization to mitigate overfitting, ensuring robust generalization across varying field lighting conditions.
> Optimization & Loss: Engineered using the Adam optimizer with categorical cross-entropy loss metrics, achieving high accuracy thresholds on agricultural validation data.
2. Full-Stack Deployment (Flask Framework)
Instead of remaining isolated in a Jupyter Notebook, the model is fully wrapped in a micro-web framework:
>Asynchronous Inference API: A lightweight Python Flask backend handles incoming HTTP POST requests, reading raw image files directly into memory buffers.
>Tensor Ingestion: Images are automatically preprocessed, resized to matching tensor dimensions, normalized, and fed into the active TensorFlow inference instance.
>Dynamic JSON Response: The backend returns precise class probabilities and diagnostic labels asynchronously to the client interface.
3. Client Interface (HTML5 / CSS3 / JavaScript)
> Responsive Layout: A modern, mobile-friendly interface designed for seamless operation on smartphones out in the field.
> Dynamic DOM Updating: Utilizes JavaScript Fetch API to securely transmit crop imagery to the backend server and render diagnostic feedback in real time without refreshing the web page.

**###🛠️ Directory Structure**
AgroVision-AI/
│
├── app.py                  # Core Flask server handling model loading and API endpoints
├── model/
│   └── agrovision_model.h5 # Trained TensorFlow/Keras weights and architecture
│
├── templates/
│   └── index.html          # Responsive web interface UI
│
├── static/
│   ├── css/
│   │   └── style.css       # Clean, modern user interface styling
│   └── js/
│       └── main.js         # Fetch API handling async image uploads and response rendering
│
└── requirements.txt        # Production dependency log (TensorFlow, Flask, NumPy)
**###📊 Mathematical Foundations & Training Methodology**

The development of AgroVision-AI is heavily rooted in advanced linear algebra and multivariate calculus frameworks:
>Dimensionality Reduction: Leveraging Principal Component Analysis (PCA) methodologies to understand feature spacing and variance distribution within the high-dimensional image matrices.

>Gradient Optimization: Utilizing multi-dimensional partial derivatives to map error surfaces, ensuring stable weights convergence through backpropagation.
**###🔮 Future Roadmap: Bounding Boxes & Drone Integration**
The next evolution of AgroVision-AI focuses on shifting from static web classification to active, autonomous physical deployment:

>**Object Detection Upgrade**: Transitioning from image classification to localized object detection models (YOLO architectures) to output precise bounding boxes around infected leaves.

>**Autonomous Hardware Deployment**: Compiling the model pipeline into specialized edge-computing hardware (like NVIDIA Jetson Nano boards) designed for installation on autonomous greenhouse monitoring drones. This setup will enable real-time, low-latency field scanning and automated spraying loops.

instances.overview: This model is a fine-tuned variant of Google's pre-trained MobileNet-V2 architecture, optimized for lightweight, low-latency image classification tasks. The base model's feature extraction layers—pretrained on the extensive ImageNet dataset—were frozen to retain fundamental spatial features (edges, textures, and shapes). Custom dense and dropout regularization layers were then appended and trained on highly specific domain data to adapt the model for high-accuracy localized classifications.

# Model Summary

This model predicts monthly temperature change values across 247 countries and regions from 1961-2023 using FAOSTAT climate data. Trained on 241k records with XGBoost regression, it captures spatial, seasonal, and temporal trends for climate monitoring and anomaly detection. Intended for researchers and policymakers needing rapid temperature change estimates.

# Model Characteristics

- **Algorithm:** xgboost_regressor
- **Problem type:** regression
- **Target column:** Value
- **Training samples:** 231,633
- **Features:** 5

# Data Overview

Trained on the Kaggle dataset [sevgisarac/temperature-change](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sevgisarac/temperature-change). Drop rows with missing target Value (4.24%). Encode high-cardinality Area (247 categories) and Area Code (M49) with target encoding; one-hot encode Months (17 categories). Treat Months Code as cyclical numerical feature by adding sin/cos transformations. Parse Year as datetime (YYYY-01-01) and derive year numeric trend; no missing values in features.

**Feature columns used:** Area Code (M49), Area, Months Code, Months, Year

# Evaluation Results

Evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation, compared against a naive baseline.

| | Model | Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| RMSE (mean) | 0.8628 | 1.0574 |
| RMSE (std) | 0.0066 | 0.0059 |

Metric direction: lower is better.

# Model Summary

The **Deepfake Dual-Stream Model (EfficientNet + DCT)** is a hybrid deep learning framework engineered to authenticate multimedia content in low-bandwidth environments. Traditional deepfake detectors fail when confronted with heavily compressed media typical of platforms like WhatsApp or Facebook. This model mitigates that "Generalization Gap" by evaluating data across two simultaneous domains:

1. **Spatial Stream:** Extracts visual blending anomalies and unnatural textures using an EfficientNetB0 backbone.
2. **Frequency Stream:** Extracts algorithmic grid structures and synthetic fingerprints utilizing a 2D Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) mapped to a custom CNN.

The model achieves a **95.00% accuracy** and **94.00% recall** on heavily compressed media, making it highly viable for social engineering security, digital forensics, and edge-adjacent deployment.

## Usage

This model is designed to process individual facial frames extracted from videos or images. It expects a dual-input format (Spatial RGB and Frequency DCT).

### Code Snippet: Loading and Inference

```python
import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np
import cv2

# 1. Load the pre-trained Dual-Stream model
model = tf.keras.models.load_model('hybrid_deepfake_model.h5')

# 2. Assume `face_crop` is an RGB image (e.g., 224x224x3) extracted via MTCNN
# Prepare Spatial Input (Raw [0, 255] RGB)
spatial_input = cv2.resize(face_crop, (224, 224))
spatial_input = np.expand_dims(spatial_input, axis=0) 

# Prepare Frequency Input (Scaled [0, 1] DCT Grayscale)
gray_face = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.resize(face_crop, (224, 224)), cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY)
float_face = np.float32(gray_face) / 255.0
dct_result = cv2.dct(float_face)
# Add channel and batch dimensions
frequency_input = np.expand_dims(np.expand_dims(dct_result, axis=-1), axis=0)

# 3. Predict
predictions = model.predict({'spatial_input': spatial_input, 'frequency_input': frequency_input})
confidence_real = predictions[0][0]
confidence_fake = predictions[0][1]

print(f"Fake Confidence: {confidence_fake * 100:.2f}%")

```

### Inputs and Outputs

* **Input 1 (`spatial_input`)**: `(None, 224, 224, 3)` — Raw RGB image array. **Note:** Do not scale to `[0, 1]` manually; the EfficientNetB0 backbone handles its own internal rescaling.
* **Input 2 (`frequency_input`)**: `(None, 224, 224, 1)` — 2D DCT array scaled `[0, 1]` derived from a grayscale conversion of the input face.
* **Output (`classification_output`)**: `(None, 2)` — Softmax probabilities representing `[Real, Fake]`.

### Known and Preventable Failures

* **Facial Occlusion:** The model relies on accurate facial bounding boxes. It will fail or output garbage data if passed full, uncropped video frames, or if the subject's face is heavily occluded (masks, extreme angles, severe low-lighting) where MTCNN fails to detect a face.

## System

This is the core inference engine of a larger decoupled system (a FastAPI backend and a Next.js frontend).

* **Input Requirements:** Downstream pipelines *must* use a facial detection algorithm (e.g., MTCNN or RetinaFace) to crop the face prior to feeding it into this model.
* **Downstream Dependencies:** For video analysis, this model evaluates single frames. A downstream aggregator (like a Max-Voting sequence logic) is required to parse multiple frame predictions into a final "Video is Fake" verdict.

## Implementation Requirements

* **Training Hardware:** Google Colab instance utilizing an NVIDIA T4 GPU (16GB VRAM).
* **Training Software:** Python 3.12, TensorFlow/Keras 2.15.
* **Training Compute:** The model utilized an `EarlyStopping` callback and halted optimally at Epoch 21 out of a maximum of 30 epochs.
* **Inference Compute:** Highly optimized for CPU inference. When thread-locked to a single CPU core (to prevent OOM errors on cloud containers), it runs at **9.56 ms/frame** (approx. 104.63 FPS throughput), consuming a peak of ~430 MB RAM (inclusive of OpenCV and MTCNN overheads).

# Model Characteristics

## Model Initialization

This is a Hybrid model combining Transfer Learning and training from scratch:

* **Spatial Stream:** Fine-tuned from a pre-trained **EfficientNetB0** model (ImageNet weights). The bottom layers were frozen to prevent catastrophic forgetting, while the top 5 layers were unfrozen for fine-tuning.
* **Frequency Stream:** Custom Convolutional Neural Network trained entirely from scratch to interpret 2D-DCT coefficients.

## Model Stats

* **Total Size:** 199.15 MB (Saved as an HDF5 `.h5` file).
* **Latency:** ~9.56 ms per frame (measured on standard CPU architecture).
* **Overfitting Mitigation:** Utilizes aggressive dropout (0.6 rate) on the fusion concatenation layer to enforce generalization and prevent mode collapse.

## Other Details

The model is currently unpruned and unquantized (Float32). To preserve Explainable AI (XAI) capabilities, the architecture supports `tf.GradientTape` on the final convolutional layer of the EfficientNet backbone, enabling live Grad-CAM heatmap generation.

# Data Overview

## Training Data

The model was trained on the **Celeb-DF v2** dataset, chosen for its high-quality, realistic deepfakes that lack obvious visual blending errors.

* **Pre-processing / Augmentation:** To simulate the real-world operational environment, the dataset was piped through a programmatic "Social Media Wash" using FFmpeg. Training media was actively degraded by applying:
1. Resolution downscaling to 360p.
2. H.264 Codec compression via a Constant Rate Factor (CRF) of 28.
3. Spatial data augmentation including Random Flip, Zoom (up to 10%), and Rotation (up to 5%).



## Demographic Groups

The training data primarily inherits the demographics of the Celeb-DF v2 dataset, which is largely comprised of celebrity interview footage. Consequently, the dataset contains predominantly Western/Caucasian facial features, though it does include some multi-ethnic diversity.

## Evaluation Data

The dataset was split using an **80% Training / 20% Testing** ratio.

* **Notable Differences:** While the model was trained on compressed data, it was rigorously benchmarked to ensure the "Generalization Gap" between pristine, high-definition data and heavily compressed (CRF 28) data remained negligible (measured at only ~3.5% performance drop).

# Evaluation Results

## Summary

The model demonstrates elite performance on degraded media, significantly outperforming purely spatial baseline models when subjected to low-bandwidth environments.

* **Accuracy:** 95.00%
* **Precision:** 96.00%
* **Recall (Sensitivity):** 94.00%
* **Specificity:** 96.25%
* **F1-Score:** 95.00%

## Subgroup Evaluation Results

Analysis was conducted on clean vs. compressed data subgroups. Traditional spatial networks often suffer a 20% - 30% drop in accuracy when exposed to social media compression. By anchoring to the DCT frequency space, this Dual-Stream model narrowed that generalization gap to roughly 3.5%, maintaining its 95% baseline on highly degraded artifacts.

## Fairness

Given the security and anti-fraud intent of this system, fairness was evaluated heavily on the **Recall (Sensitivity)** metric (94.00%). In a forensic context, minimizing False Negatives (allowing a deepfake to pass as authentic) is the highest priority. Demographic fairness is highly dependent on the initial MTCNN face localization; if MTCNN fails to accurately crop darker skin tones in low lighting, the pipeline will systematically skip those frames.

## Usage Limitations

**No Audio Detection:** This model analyzes strictly visual and frequency-based image data. It cannot detect AI-generated voice cloning, which is frequently paired with deepfakes.
* **Single-Frame Context:** The Keras model does not possess temporal memory (like an LSTM). Unnatural flickering between frames must be calculated by the downstream system aggregator, not the model itself.

## Ethics

**Privacy & Zero-Retention:** Deepfake analysis inherently deals with sensitive biometric data (human faces). This model was engineered to be deployed in a "Zero-Retention" pipeline, where images are processed entirely in temporary memory and strictly deleted post-inference to comply with NDPR and GDPR regulations.

**XAI Transparency:** To mitigate the ethical risks of "Black Box" AI making unchecked decisions about media authenticity, the network's spatial backbone supports Grad-CAM. This allows the system to generate heatmaps highlighting *why* a face was flagged (e.g., pointing out pixel anomalies near the jawline), allowing human reviewers to ultimately verify the model's judgment.

## Overview
This model predicts the magnitude of a seismic event given its geographic
location (latitude, longitude) and depth. It was trained on a self-collected
USGS earthquake dataset spanning 2020–2024 (140K records).

## Features Used
- latitude
- longitude
- depth (km)

Features like `tsunami`, `sig`, and `alert` present in the raw USGS data were
deliberately excluded, as they are determined *after* an event's magnitude is
known and would introduce data leakage.

## Performance
- RMSE: 0.40
- R²: 0.79 (on held-out test data, 80/20 split)

## Intended Use
This model estimates the *expected magnitude of a hypothetical seismic event*
at a given location/depth, based on historical patterns. It does not predict
whether or when an earthquake will occur.

## Limitations
With only 3 geographic features, the model captures general regional seismic
tendencies but cannot account for real-time seismic wave data, fault
mechanics, or other geophysical signals that would improve precision further.

## Training Data
Self-collected USGS Earthquake dataset (2020-2024), also published on Kaggle:
https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/adarshsalukhe/earthquakes-2020-2024

instances.overview: The model is Base Model, Fine Tunable
instances.usage:
Scenario: Suppose a seismic sensor detects an event near the coast of California (latitude 34.05, longitude -118.24) at a depth of 10 km.
Feed these three values latitude, longitude, depth into the model. It looks at the 140,000 historical earthquakes it was trained on and finds that events occurring at similar coordinates and similar depth have historically clustered around a certain magnitude range.
Based on that pattern, the model outputs a predicted magnitude of approximately 4.1.
This doesn't mean an earthquake of magnitude 4.1 will happen there it means if a seismic event occurs at this location and depth, historical data suggests its magnitude would likely be around 4.1, give or take 0.4 (the model's average error margin).
